newsitem.title: USA: Baseball's Schott forced to sell car dealership.
newsitem.headline: Baseball's Schott forced to sell car dealership.

text.p: Cincinnati Reds owner Marge Schott has agreed to sell her auto dealership and head off the threat that General Motors would strip her of the business because she falsified vehicle sales, a television station reported Tuesday.
WCPO-TV said the 68-year-old widow reached agreement "in principle" to sell her dealership to the Joseph family, which owns some other local GM dealerships.
No terms were disclosed. Mrs. Schott has had the dealership for 16 years.

Schott, under Major League suspension until 1998 from operating the baseball club, faced a hearing Feb. 13 before the State Auto Dealers Board on a complaint by General Motors that she falsified the sales in 1995 in order to meet a GM quota needed to retain her dealership franchise.
General Motors alleged last month, in documents filed with the state of Ohio, that Schott falsified sales records in 1995 at a Chevrolet dealership she owned when it failed to meet sales criteria.
GM wanted to terminate Schott, 68, as a GM dealer and said the dealership performed poorly for 10 years.
If GM approved the sale, the hearing would be unnecessary because its purpose was to determine if she should be allowed to keep the Chevrolet-Geo dealership in suburban Montgomery.
National League President Leonard Coleman said last week that Major League Baseball would review GM's allegations against Schott and take "appropriate action as warranted."

In a document filed with the state of Ohio's Bureau of Motor Vehicles Dealers Board, which oversees dealer licensing, GM alleged: "Schott's reported sales included false sales reports, including 57 'sales' in which Schott simply fabricated 'purchasers' that never bought a vehicle."
She used names of friends and dealership personnel as buyers, then hid the cars on her estate, selling at least one later as a used car, GM said.
Schott was suspended by Major League Baseball for making several racially insensitive statements, including praise for the early years of Adolf Hitler's Nazi dictatorship.
